analysis.title: Macro Derivs Flow: AI de-risking / Upside Risk Management / Sell AUD / Quiet Gold
key_insights: US institutional flows were dominated by selling, with Semis, Neoclouds and crowded AI/momentum exposures the main sources of funds. Thursday's bounce was sold as investors returned to de-risking and adding shorts.

Buying was selective rather than a broad re-grossing, with demand for Pharma/Biotech on PB and pockets in Cyber, Consumer and non-AI Industrials. Retail were net sellers of single stocks, while ETF demand held up better in QQQ and Healthcare.

US options flows showed sizable tactical upside demand consistent with positioning for a potential squeeze. QQQ upside was added via December call condors and January outright calls, plus SPX call spreads, alongside SPY downside hedging and some closing sales of upside structures.
Korea and Taiwan remained focal points of Asia AI de-risking. Korea saw KRW5.2tn of foreign selling over the week, partly absorbed by retail, and Taiwan's weekly visible pad was 65% seller-skewed.
Korea saw early-week protection buying on the derivatives desk, while Taiwan protection was unwound toward the end of the week.

Japan cash was quieter and moderately seller-skewed (56% better to sell). Derivatives were two-way, with early protection buying giving way to downside unwinds, NKY upside demand, then put rolls, vol selling and overwriting into Friday's weakness.

HK/CN cash flows turned seller-skewed, with Internet and Metals/Miners under pressure and domestic semiconductor substitution a pocket of buying. The derivatives desk continued to see CSI300/CSI1000 upside demand, seen by US clients as a cheap way to express China upside.

In FX, AUD selling was the clearer conviction trade, with HFs selling AUD on all ten trading days in the Flow Monitor window and NOK selling accelerating. Broad USD buying was modest despite the dollar rally, and the options desk saw interest in AUDUSD downside structures.

The gold selloff showed neither broad holder capitulation nor much marginal buying. Physical demand was subdued, ETF holdings resilient, CTAs short, and Friday saw options hedge close-outs and some topside structures at lower spot.
